newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96/97 copper output seen rising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96/97 copper output seen rising.

text.p: Australian copper mine output is seen rising in the year to 495,000 tonnes in the year to June 30, 1997, up from a previous estimate of 490,000, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

The Australian government's main commodity forecasting agency, in its December quarter report, also raised its estimate for Australian refined copper production to 326,000 tonnes from 300,000 in the September quarter.
The 1996/97 copper mine estimate is 9.5 percent up on the 452,000 tonnes produced in 1995/96, ABARE said.
The higher output is mainly due to increased output from existing mines, the report said.
ABARE said export earnings were forecast to increase by nearly 11 percent to A$1.03 billion in 1996/97.
"Substantially higher export volumes are expected to more than offset the effects on earnings of lower prices and an assumed stronger Australian dolllar," ABARE said.

The bureau said world copper production is expected to rise to 13.08 million tonnes in calendar 1997, from the 12.27 million estimated for 1996. It said world output is expected to rise due to mine or metal output increases in Chile, the United States,
Japan, Peru Indonesia, Germany, Spain and Australia.
ABARE said consumption is forecast to rise to 12.52 million tonnes in calendar 1997, compared with an estimated 12.10 million in 1996, up from the 11.82 million consumed in 1995.
The bureau said copper stocks were expected to rise to 920,000 tonnes in 1997, from an estimated 630,000 tonnes in 1996 and 650,000 tonnes in 1995.

"The stocks situation is expected to turn around in 1997. With world production of copper forecast to grow faster than consumption, total stocks are forecast to rise to the equivalent of 4.4 weeks consumption by the end of 1997," ABARE said.

ABARE said copper prices were likely to continue to fall in calendar 1997 following weaker prices in 1996. It said prices are estimated to average US$2100 per tonne in 1997, down from an estimated $2285 in 1996 and $2936 in 1995.

"The scope for substantial upward movement in prices is expected to be constrained by further liquidation of outstanding long positions and producer forward sales in expectation of price falls in the second half of 1997," ABARE said.
